rationale: This is a tiny, pointer- and recursion-heavy Olden benchmark (11 functions, ~2 KB text) whose hot path is HashLookup/HashInsert inside the MST blue-rule traversal, so the table favors low-overhead passes and penalizes expensive ones. SUB, SPLIT, and IGV get low Runtime/Size/CorrectnessRisk weights since instruction substitution, block splitting, and global-reference indirection cost little while meaningfully raising static-analysis effort in such a small binary where every function (MakeGraph, MakeHash, Do_all_BlueRule, HashInsert) is worth obfuscating. BCF carries deliberately high RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights (0.7) because bogus control flow inflates a 2 KB binary quickly and the hash-lookup inner loop is hot, limiting it to functions where its security payoff is largest; FLA gets a moderate penalty plus a notable CorrectnessRisk weight (0.5) since flattening the recursive Do_all_BlueRule and pointer-dense graph construction risks subtle breakage even though its control-flow hiding is the strongest single defense. ICALL and IBR carry moderate cost weights (0.5-0.6) so they are applied selectively to the call/branch sites that matter (hash dispatch, blue-rule recursion) rather than program-wide, keeping runtime within the benchmark's acceptable envelope while maximizing diversity across all five obfuscation dimensions.
